newsitem.title: GERMANY: D.Telekom domestic market share slips.
newsitem.headline: D.Telekom domestic market share slips.

text.p: Europe's largest telecommunications company Deutsche Telekom AG said on Tuesday its share of the domestic market slipped slightly last year as competition began to step up ahead of full deregulation in 1998.
"Telekom's share of the domestic market declined from 86 percent to 84 percent, but we still increased revenues," said the company's chief finance officer Joachim Kroeske.

A combination of increased competition, particularly from call-back services, price cuts and efforts by customers to save on international calls caused revenue from outgoing international calls to plunge 18.6 percent last year to 4.8 billion marks ($2.8 billion).
"This was primarily the result of price cuts, particularly on the U.S. route," Kroeske told the annual news conference.

Telekom chairman Ron Sommer appeared unconcerned about the rate of domestic market share decline in 1996, saying this would be offset by a rising share of the international market and increased volumes in Germany.
"Competition creates growth," he said. "I expect a continued moderate market development and I will say again, we intend to fight for every customer," he said.
Sommer would not be drawn on forecasts for the company's domestic market share over the next few years.
"I don't want to make it any easier for our competitors," he said.
As the deadline for the opening of telecoms markets throughout Europe on January 1 approaches, Telekom is improving service and preparing new price intiatives.

"We are preparing a number of interesting tariffs for customers," said Detlav Buchal, board member for residential customers, adding that there would be a special focus on customers with a monthly call volume of over 500 marks.

On the service side, Telekom has improved the speed of installations. Around 73 percent of installations were made with ten days in 1996. While most customers must still wait days for repairs, the company's goal is to repair any service disruptions within one day. ($ = 1.698 German Marks)
